coherence.reasons: Both run a consistent chain from governing thought to action titles, with the same core numbers behind them. Y's Whether / Route / How structure maps directly onto the decision question, and each executive-summary line is carried by one slide with a derivation. Its hypothesis-test slide ties the storyline to four conditions and then to five board decisions. X is also logically ordered (market, A passes, B fails, ad cost swings, how to launch). But its summary says Japan becomes the better choice above 28.6% ACoS, while its own slide 31 shows Japan ahead on cash at any ACoS above plan. It also claims 'most new spend is going to Korean brands' beside its own 38.6% share-of-growth figure. Y's '$40M is not reachable within the limits' sits explicitly in the hierarchy, where X leaves it as a footnoted reading.

judgment.reasons: Both reach the key's preferred conclusion: Amazon-led with gates, reject retail-led, Japan as fallback, retail trigger raised to 20% awareness. Y weighs the trade-offs more fully. It states that no route reaches $40M within the limits and asks the board to restate the ambition. It names the payback-versus-ambition trade-off and asks the board to pre-agree whether a slip to 2031–32 is acceptable, flagging this as a departure from the limit. It derives green/amber/red thresholds from the model (28.6% breakeven, 34.4% zero-profit point), adjusts them for the tariff, and sizes exposure at Gate 1 ($1.9–2.9M). It considers waiting a year, and adds a door test with a measured halo before any roll-out. X's gates are sensible, but its single ACoS threshold of 28.6% sits below the 32% benchmark it expects, with only a vague response ('cut ad budget; prepare Japan fallback'). X treats the $40M gap mainly as a matter of timing and leaves the ambition reading as a footnote for the board to confirm.

evidence.reasons: Both reproduce the key calculations correctly: $4.73 and $7.55 unit contributions, Option A at +$2.40M / +$0.38M / −$2.32M, the 28.6% breakeven, Option B at −$20.8M and 4.5% margin, and the tariff effect. Both critique the 4.5 units per door and the correlation, and neither uses the $5.2B figure. Y adds the CAGR (17.3% vs 5.1%), a volume-by-ACoS grid, breakeven under the tariff (27.0%), the US-versus-Japan cash crossover (~26%), a plausibility check on the 300k volume, Option B on realistic inputs ($26.4M), and what Option B would need to pay back (3.1× halo or 23.5 units per door). It also notes that two of three Amazon-first peers stalled. X has the fuller correlation critique (reverse cause, common cause, a fair test) and a clean ACoS-by-duty table. But X makes several unsupported or wrong inferences: 'most new spend is going to Korean brands' against 38.6%; 'US buyers rate it as Korean buyers do' with no Korean rating data; monthly growth as 'a sign of word of mouth'; and 'the pilot understates what a full range can do'. Y's 'Amazon is where most of it is bought' at 41% is a minor overstatement.

revision.reasons: Both keep the CEO's Amazon-first hypothesis with conditions, which is what the key expects. Both raise the awareness trigger from 15% to 20% using the 3.5-versus-4.0 evidence, and both replace the assumed 25% ACoS with a gate at the breakeven. Y is more systematic. It breaks the hypothesis into four testable conditions with a verdict on each (two hold, one conditional, one fails). It keeps the $10M Amazon trigger and says so, adds a 12-month door test and a measured halo, turns the dated 2029 retail commitment into an earned option, and resets the $40M ambition. X's 'holds with three changes' slide covers similar ground (trigger, ad-cost gate, targeted door test) but is less explicit about which parts are kept and does not reset the ambition as firmly.

overall.reasons: Both documents are strong and reach the defensible recommendation with accurate modelling against the board's constraints. Y would serve the board better. It turns the analysis into specific decisions: approve Stage 1, adopt derived gate thresholds, pre-agree the payback slip, restate the ambition, and replace the retail trigger. It says plainly that $40M by 2030 is not reachable within the limits. It tests volume as well as ACoS and tariff, and it handles the likely case that ACoS lands between pilot and benchmark with an amber zone rather than a single tripwire. X is thorough and has the better correlation critique and tariff table, but it is longer, carries a few unsupported inferences, and is softer on the ambition trade-off and on what happens when the ACoS gate is missed.
